rationale: Later review reports a positive unstimulated saliva difference for oral asparagus preparation with mecobalamin. Original Chinese trial remains unavailable and the review classifies high risk of bias. No drooling or steamed-asparagus contrast.
The Indian smell identification test uses a cardamom odor stimulus. Accuracy describes existing olfactory impairment and supplies no ingestion effect.
An eight-oil cystitis product includes thyme. The abstract reports void frequency rather than a separate urgency endpoint, without culinary preparation or an isolated thyme comparison.
Both species were screened in vitro. The human cognitive and mental-fatigue comparison used Mentha × piperita essential oil. No fresh spearmint Parkinson fatigue contrast.

Multi-component pillow with spearmint is described for insomnia and cerebral fatigue. The abstract gives no oral intake or controlled patient fatigue data. Full patent page not returned in this route.
Mixed dried pillow ingredients include spearmint. Fatigue is a product claim. No human efficacy comparison or ingestion. Full patent page not returned in this route.
Method claim for a mixed herbal drink. The description supplies no controlled fresh-spearmint Parkinson fatigue comparison.
Fragrance and wet tissue formulation includes oil and scent components. No dietary spearmint intervention with fatigue outcome.
Acute study of extracted Amomum subulatum in healthy adults, a separate species and formulation from ground green cardamom.
Separate 14-day test of black cardamom fruit extract reports favorable selected early attention measures. Species, preparation and population differ.
Spice heavy-metal concentrations and risk estimates. It gives no cardamom-specific clinical attention contrast.
Isolated capsaicin in rat stroke and neurological tests. No ground cayenne exposure or observed human falls.
The summary covers capsaicin for postherpetic pain and a separate Tai Chi falls study. These links do not assign capsaicin to the falls outcomes.
Review centers on pain treatment injection techniques. It does not establish dietary cayenne and measured fall frequency.
Capsaicin appears in an evoked nociception model. Rotarod and beam behaviors concern separate effects of nerve injury and tested analgesics, with no culinary cayenne falls comparison.
A healthy volunteer oral canola crossover measured paced tapping. It found no significant rate variation across trials and no significant motor-region BOLD change.
BOLD attenuated during an instructed tapping task after oral canola in a separate study. The paper provides no task-performance contrast.
Long-term neurological findings follow toxic oil exposure in the 1981 epidemic. This is not a refined canola meal or isolated clinical dexterity intervention.
The isolated seed-extract groups show no clear catalepsy difference at either tested level. Biochemical and toxicity work on the multiple-herb product supplies no separate motor outcome.
Oral isolated thymoquinone reduced chlorpromazine catalepsy and improved locomotor proxies. Full exact tables open and no ground seed comparison.
